accuracy.evidence: The statutory wording 'use the first two or three letters of a word to check its spelling in a dictionary' was checked against the National Curriculum in England, English Years 3-4 spelling, and the Common Core references against L.2.2e and L.3.2g. Every alphabetical claim was checked by code: the three lists sort to bag-bed-big-box-bus, cake-city-cow-crab-cup and shark-shed-ship-shop-shut; each filing word falls between exactly one pair of guide words (bad-bell, bike-boot, brick-bus); each hunt word lies on exactly one of the ten pages; entry lists are in order (fridge, friend, fright, frog; sense, sentence, separate, set). Spellings friend, beautiful, different, sentence, school, knife, phone and write match the Oxford Children's Dictionary.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the known errors: ordering by the first letter only (prediction 'bus, they both start with b', challenge 'first', feedback naming the deciding letter), believing a word must be a guide word to be on a page (prediction 'No, bed is not a guide word'), turning the wrong way (hunt feedback 'comes after boot. Go later', challenge 'back'), stopping at an entry that starts the same (look step 'fright starts the same, but it is a different word'), letter swaps (challenge 'ie', m6) and giving up when the first sound has another spelling (prediction 'It is not a real word', challenge 'give', p5, m8).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdict models a dictionary itself: pages with guide words in the corners that accept only words falling between them, a ten-page book the learner navigates with Earlier / On this page / Later, an entry list for a misspelling's first two letters, and a missing-word page that only resolves when a different first grapheme (sch, kn, ph, wr) is dragged in. flagabc teaches letter names and flagdefine writes definitions; neither uses guide words or page navigation. The lab_distinct gate passed under the 30% similarity limit.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule by doing: the order step refuses bus before bag and names the second letter that decides it, filing refuses a page and says whether the word falls before the first or after the last guide word, the hunt counts page turns so comparing with guide words visibly beats flicking, and the missing-word step only succeeds when another spelling of the first sound is tried. Completion lines restate the rule ('Guide words tell you which way to turn').

predictions.evidence: Three predictions have tempting wrong options that the lab then disproves: 'bus, they both start with b' (disproved when bag must be tapped first), 'No, bed is not a guide word' (disproved when bed files onto the bad-bell page) and 'It is not a real word' for skool (disproved when dragging sch reveals school).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Eleven wrong-answer messages keyed to the slip: first-letter-only ordering (first), word before the first guide word (before), after the last (after), giving up (give), keeping the wrong spelling of the sound (one), turning back (back), staying put (stay), looking up last letters (end), reading every page (every), swapped ie (ie) and a missing letter (miss). Six questions rotate so a retry gives a new item.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences, one idea each (ABC order beyond the first letter, guide words, checking every letter, another spelling of the first sound); the validator's family readability limits passed for kid and adult text. Lab prompts are short ('Find frog. 0 page turns so far.'). The adult text uses the precise terms alphabetical order, guide words, catchwords, entry and headword.

no_filler.evidence: No warm-up text; the content gate found no banned phrases and explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson. Each feedback line gives the deciding fact, for example 'skool is not there, but school is, with sch' and 'bus comes after bell because u comes after e'.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 screenshots in dark theme for all 6 steps: the five order slots and word cards fit one row at 390 px, the three guide-word pages share the width with 13 px guide words still readable, the hunt page and its three Earlier / On this page / Later keys are large, the four entries sit in a 2 by 2 grid, and the sch, kn, ph, wr keys fit one row. Every action is repeated as a full-size button under the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed all five tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) reported no violations in light or dark. Buttons carry spoken labels such as 'File on page bad to bell', 'The right spelling is friend' and 'Start with sch', and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback message.

sources: National Curriculum in England: English programmes of study, Years 3-4 spelling (statutory: use the first two or three letters of a word to check its spelling in a dictionary)
Common Core State Standards ELA L.2.2e and L.3.2g (consult reference materials, including beginning dictionaries, to check and correct spellings)
Oxford Children's Dictionary (Oxford University Press), guide words and entries for the example words
